visual_argument: A patient record is a card at one measured size, and the one added line is a strip of ember tape laid on it: two matched cards stand in a pool of light, three sorting trays put the notched card of the patient who later deteriorated in front, and with the tape laid on, that card drops to the back slot, nearly ten in a hundred times, until the tape is peeled back at the close.
build_risk: Frame 7 is a steel index card drawer of 100 upright cards at 0.25 mm each with ten notched, taped cards pushed behind a tabbed divider and leaning back so each tape takes the key. A hundred thin card tops merge into one block at 432 px and a low key shades each card with the next. The build answer is a drawer run across the sun, a dark gap at the divider, the ten leaning at 20 degrees with their faces turned into the key, cards built as instanced rounded boxes in the chassis, and the shadow box sized to the drawer. If one repair fails, the ten move to a separate rank behind the drawer and the hundred are counted as ten blocks of ten.
